chosen_format_rationale: CycloneDX 1.6 has first-class component types file and data (markdown skills as data; Python/hooks as file) plus SHA-256 hashes and occurrence paths. SPDX 2.3 File can also list paths and checksums but has no data type. This program's IMP-0062 already names CycloneDX for the plugin closure.

claims.claim: CycloneDX 1.6 can express this package's markdown skills as type=data and its Python tools/hooks as type=file, each with a SHA-256 hash and an occurrence path.

source_lineage.snippet: type.enum includes "file" and "data"; properties include cpe, purl, swid. Captured schema has no prompt-injection or instruction-semantics field.

source_lineage.name: cdx-use-cases
source_lineage.snippet: By utilizing identifiers such as CPE, PURL, and SWID, CycloneDX enables the detection of known vulnerabilities in components, facilitating proactive risk management.

claims.strongest_caveat: The schema permits file/data; many lockfile-oriented generators never emit those types. This draft is hand-classified from the tree, not from cdxgen/syft (neither is installed here).

claims.canonical_mechanism: SPDX File Information (clause 8) + JSON schema files.items
claims.claim: SPDX 2.3 File can name a markdown/Python path with checksums (integrity of bytes) and licenses; it does not have a file type for 'skill prompt' or 'hook script semantics'.

source_lineage.name: spdx-2.3-schema
source_lineage.snippet: files.items.required=["SPDXID","checksums","fileName"]; checksums description: verify that the contents of a File or Package have not changed. fileTypes enum includes OTHER, DOCUMENTATION, SOURCE, TEXT — no skill/prompt type. packages.required=["SPDXID","downloadLocation","name"].

source_lineage.name: spdx-2.3-file-info
source_lineage.snippet: Checksum algorithms consume data from the file and produce a short, fix-sized summary that is sensitive to changes in the file's data. 8.4.2 Intent: Checksum values are used primarily to protect a file's data against accidental corruption during transmissions or storage. Cryptographically strong checksum algorithms may be used to detect deliberate corruption, but only if the authenticity of the checksum value may be verified.

claims.strongest_caveat: SPDX 3.0 adds more element types; this unit measured 2.3 because that is the JSON schema that fetched cleanly as the structured rail.

claims.canonical_mechanism: schema field inventory + CycloneDX PURL/CPE identity use case
claims.claim: Neither format's first-class fields detect prompt-injection or hostile instructions in a listed markdown skill. Vulnerability matching in CycloneDX is specified via CPE/PURL/SWID, which a first-party SKILL.md does not have.

lockfile_root.note: Repo root has package.json and package-lock.json (npm workspaces). A lockfile-only SBOM of the product root lists those npm packages (count=7) and still captures zero markdown skills, hooks, or first-party Python tools.

uncaptured.title: Hostile instruction / prompt-injection in a hash-listed markdown skill
uncaptured.why_sbom_misses_it: CycloneDX records type/name/hash/path. Vulnerability matching needs CPE/PURL/SWID. A first-party SKILL.md has no ecosystem PURL, and the BOM does not carry file body or instruction semantics. A skill whose SHA-256 is listed is 'in inventory' even when its markdown tells the agent to ignore prior instructions.

evidence_requirement_compliance.rule: every claim carries TWO mechanically independent rails (structured schema probe AND prose source), each with permalink, fetch timestamp, HTTP status, sha256

failed_fetch_pivot.pivot: CISA SBOM page HTML (verbatim nested-inventory quote)
failed_fetch_pivot.second_attempt_same_class: CISA SBOM FAQ 2024 PDF captured (HTTP 200) but Flate-compressed body is not quoted as a rail here; C5 uses the CISA HTML page already captured as the prose rail.

named_uncaptured_risk.result: The hostile SKILL.md is present in the draft SBOM as type=data with a matching SHA-256. The hostile marker is absent from the BOM. vulnerabilities=[]. No property detects prompt-injection. The SBOM therefore lists the risk-bearing file and does not capture the risk.
named_uncaptured_risk.title: Hostile instruction / prompt-injection in a hash-listed markdown skill

protecting_against.answer: Listed-file integrity (SHA-256 mismatch / substitution of a path already in the BOM) and, when a component has a CPE/PURL/SWID, lookup of known library vulnerabilities and license identity. Not first-party markdown-skill instructions, not PreToolUse hook execution privilege, not secrets inside a file whose hash is listed.
protecting_against.question: protecting against what?

question: Do SPDX and CycloneDX express anything meaningful about a package of markdown skills, shell hooks and Python tools - and if the components are not libraries, what is the SBOM actually protecting against here?

reviewer.notes: Refuter required a live hostile SKILL.md whose hash is in the BOM while the instruction is not a finding. Claims C1-C5 survived that control. Strongest leftover caveat: a different generator that only walks lockfiles would miss the payload entirely (C5), which is a generator defect, not a reason to treat a lockfile SBOM as covering skills.

sentinel: SUCCESS:RES-0050 in the receipt AND a generated draft SBOM plus a named risk it fails to capture
